title: The app slice of the agent platform set-up: the service login, the tool reads of the two owners, the parameter keys and lists, the sample key, the migration numbering and the route in front of the admin reads are not fixed by any source
source: Legacy RWB-E1-058 sections 3, 4, 7, 11, 12 and 13; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.1 and A2.2; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2, T5.2, T6.2 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41, 42 and 43; Ownership Map v1 (eight agent tables owner P10, eleven P10 operations, EV-28 owner P10, AgentRunWorkflow owner P10); Template and Rules v1 §R3, §R4, §R5.5, §R7.3 and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC16 to AC20; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.8; 13 Solution plan
description: Six values the app slice needs are absent or unresolved in the sources. (1) The per-service login of rwb-agent is required by DP-02 and by the legacy section 3, which names only the agent identity RWB-DEV-SY-AGENT and its SIT, UAT and PROD equivalents; no source names the login of the service. (2) The legacy ToolGateway read another module's Java interface for the case and the document; in the target the case read and the document read are owner contracts, and no source states which operations the tool gateway calls or how a tool off the allow-list is answered. (3) The parameter keys the run reads and the code of the lists are not named, although DP-06 and DP-07 move parameters and reference data to rwb-case and the legacy section 13 held the policy and prompt rows beside the loader. (4) The unique key of agent_sample differs: the legacy section 13 fixes (agent_code, sample_code, sample_version, subject_id, label_key) while the physical schema of today declares (sample_code, sample_version, label_key). (5) Only V10_001__agent_runtime.sql is named by a source; the later migration numbers of the service, and the split of agent_feedback and agent_alert between this story and the two stories that own their behaviour, are not stated. (6) The gateway-bff route in front of the admin reads has no name and no path. The story keeps the legacy behaviour and settles each value as an assumption.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-058 section 3 ('the service identity SY-AGENT exists with the Entra ID managed identity RWB-DEV-SY-AGENT ... and the permissions seeded in Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql'), section 12 (the published interface AgentOrchestrator.run, the in-process ToolGateway, the eight operations), section 13 ('Flyway migration V10_001__agent_runtime.sql creates agent_policy, agent_prompt, agent_run, agent_sample, agent_evaluation_run and agent_evaluation' and the sample key 'unique (agent_code, sample_code, sample_version, subject_id, label_key)'); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 (the eight tables), T6.2 ('service identities for jobs and agents') and T-A.1 (eleven operations, none of them a tool call); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (rwb-agent IN: DocumentStored, CaseCreated; TMP Tool gateway: read-only calls for the agent) and slide 41 (schema rwb_agent, one login per service); Template and Rules v1 §R4 and §R5.5 DP-01, DP-06, DP-07, DP-11, DP-13, DP-15 and DP-19
area: Agent platform: identity, tool path, parameters, schema keys and route
owner_role: Solution architect with the P10 service owner and the owners of rwb-case, rwb-document and rwb-access
proposed: Name the login 'the rwb-agent login (DP-02)' until the platform agrees the string; read the case facts and the document fields through the two owner operations with one hop and the 2 s budget; read the parameter keys and the lists through the rwb-case contracts at run time; keep the legacy sample key and reconcile it with the physical schema at the build; keep V10_001__agent_runtime.sql for the six tables of this story and let the later migrations take the next numbers of the service's sequence; reach the admin reads through the gateway-bff route. Every value is settled in the assumption rows cited and no literal is invented.

title: The contract baseline of the agent platform: the event family beyond EV-28, the member types of the report and the metrics, the inputs reference of the record, the sample key and the assignment of agent_run_daily are not specified by any source
source: Legacy RWB-E1-058 section 12 and 14; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.1, A2.2, A2.5 and A2.6; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2, T3.3, T5.3 and T-A.1 to T-A.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41, 42, 43 and 44; Ownership Map v1 (eleven P10 operations, eight P10 tables, EV-28, AgentRunWorkflow); Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.5 and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC6; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.3; 12.7; 12.8; 19 Out of scope
description: Five elements of the contract are open in the sources. (1) EV-28 AgentRunCompleted is the only event the sources name on the agent topic; the family pattern rwb.agent.<Event>.v1 admits a run-started or run-failed member and no source names one, so the contract declares EV-28 only and calls any further member a new version of the topic's contract. (2) The member types of AgentEvaluationReport and AgentMetric[] are given only as names; the type and length of the inputs reference of the decision record are given by no source, and the record shape itself belongs to the decision-record library and to rwb-decision. (3) The eight agent tables are declared, but their physical keys differ from the legacy constraints on agent_sample (see CG-B-P10-01-E1058-1) and no source states whether the second and third keys of the legacy section 13 survive the move into rwb_agent. (4) agent_run_daily is named by FSD P10 v3 A2.6 in the rerun criterion of the monitor, and it is absent from the Ownership Map, from the logical model v8 and from the physical schema v6, so its owner and its key are unstated. (5) The gateway-bff route in front of the eleven operations has no name and no path, and the status code set of a feed-back operation is wider than any source states.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 43 row 28 ('AgentRunCompleted | rwb-agent | rwb.agent.events.v1 | rwb-decision, rwb-document, rwb-deviation'), slide 42 note (CloudEvents, key caseId, no personal data, BACKWARD compatibility), slide 16 (P10 OUT: rwb.agent.events.v1: AgentRunCompleted) and slide 44 (no job for the agent platform); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 (DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-111), T3.2 (the eight lists of values), T3.3 (the relationships by ID only) and T-A.2 (the eleven operations and their error sets); FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.6 AC-ALT-P10-006-02 ('agent_run_daily holds the same 2 rows for 2026-12-01'); Ownership Map v1 (no agent_run_daily row, eight agent tables and eleven P10 operations); Template and Rules v1 §R4 (event name pattern) and §R5.5 DP-03, DP-09 and DP-13
area: Contract: event family, payload member types, schema keys and the monitor table
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-agent with the solution architect and the owners of rwb-decision and rwb-case
proposed: Declare EV-28 as the only member of the family the sources name and treat any further member as a new version agreed with its consumers; fix the element names of the report and of the metrics and leave their types to the review with the owners; keep the legacy sample key; leave agent_run_daily out of the baseline and to the monitor story that names it; declare the route as a pass-through of one hop whose name is agreed with the route contract. The app, infrastructure and deployment stories and the integration copy build against these shapes and the fakes.

title: The infrastructure slice of the agent platform: the INT-23 host, port, certificate and Key Vault entry names, the login name, the partition and retention values, the worker concurrency, the budget measurement points and the alarm thresholds are not specified by any source
source: Legacy RWB-E1-058 sections 3 and 13; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.1; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T5.1, T6.2 and T7 (NFR-010); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 7, 8, 16, 35, 41, 42 and 43; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11 and 12; Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.5 and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC8; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: Six environment values of this key are absent from every source. (1) The Enterprise AI private endpoint INT-23 has no host, port, certificate subject or certificate authority named; only the approach 'private endpoint in the SCB tenant' and the frequency 'per request' are given. (2) The Key Vault entries of the model gateway call and of the login have no names, and the rwb-agent service login has no name although DP-02 requires one login per service. (3) The topic rwb.agent.events.v1 has no partition count, replication factor or retention, and the retry and .dlt topic names follow the §R4 pattern but are not written in any source. (4) The Temporal worker concurrency, poller count and activity timeouts are not given, and no source states the worker identity of rwb-agent. (5) The 60 second model budget and the 2 s client budget are targets (NFR-010, ADR-020) with no measurement point, no percentile and no alarm threshold. (6) The pod capacity, the scaling rule for a burst of runs and the operator alarms have no figures. No source names a Blob container for agent artefacts either: the policies, the prompts, the samples and the runs are rows of rwb_agent, so no container is created and none is invented.
evidence: TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T5.1 ('INT-23 | Enterprise AI model endpoint | Both | Private endpoint in the SCB tenant | Per request') and T7 (NFR-010 'An agent returns an answer within its target, after which the rule result is used and the case still routes | Under 60 seconds'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (rwb-agent OUT: 'Enterprise AI endpoint: HTTPS private endpoint'), slide 35 ('rwb-agent: 60 s, or the rule result is used'), slide 41 (schema, topic and task queue per service) and slide 43 row 28; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 11 (namespace rwb-recovery, one task queue per service, KEDA scales workers on backlog) and slide 12 (the workflow kit and 'Agent run with rule fallback'); Template and Rules v1 §R4 (topic, retry and .dlt pattern, task queue and login per service) and DP-02, DP-09 and DP-11
area: Infrastructure: private endpoint, identity and secrets, topic, queue, budgets and gates
owner_role: SCB IT infrastructure with the ACE platform team and security
proposed: Provision the private path to INT-23 with TLS and mTLS, the schema and the login with grants on rwb_agent only, the Key Vault entries of the login and of the gateway, the topic with its retry and .dlt topics and the producer ACL, the queue with the worker identity and concurrency, the two measured budgets with their alarms, the sizing and the five pipeline gates, and record every environment value as a reviewed value per environment rather than a template constant. No table, no bucket and no business value is created.

title: The deployment slice of the agent platform: the replica, resource, probe and rollout values, the alert thresholds, the ordering of the later migrations and the blue-green mechanism of the admin path are not specified by any source
source: Legacy RWB-E1-058 sections 4, 5, 13, 14 and 16; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.1 and A2.2; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T6.2 and T7; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 20 and 44; Ownership Map v1; Template and Rules v1 §R3, §R5.5, §R7.2 and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC9; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: Five deployment values of this key are absent from every source. (1) The replica counts, the resource requests and limits, the probe paths and timings, the start-up window and the rollout window are not given; the platform leaves them to the environment. (2) The alert thresholds of the fallback-rate rise, the dead-letter count, the queue backlog, the run throughput and the error rate have no figures, and no source states the window or the percentile of each. (3) The order and the numbering of the later migrations of the service are unstated beyond the baseline V10_001__agent_runtime.sql and the proposal migration of the extraction key. (4) The mechanism of the blue-green path in front of the admin operations is not named: no source states whether it is a second deployment, a second colour of the same chart or a route weight, and the only statement available is that a version load must not be interrupted. (5) The feature flags of the service other than rwb.agent.platform have no name, and the removal dates are not given. The story fixes the shape of each value and leaves every number to the environment.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-058 section 13 ('Feature flag: rwb.agent.platform') and section 14 (the seven messages); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T6.2 (single sign-on, capability area per endpoint, service identities) and T7 (NFR-008 under 2 seconds, NFR-009, NFR-010 under 60 seconds); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (every service from the service template and shared libraries), slide 8 (the edge and the route) and slide 44 (the job map, no agent job); Template and Rules v1 §R3 default ruling (feature flags to the platform library), §R5.5 DP-06 and DP-19, and §R7.2 s17
area: Operations: chart values, migration order, alert thresholds, flags and the admin rollout
owner_role: DevOps team with the ACE platform team and the owner of rwb-agent
proposed: Keep every replica, resource, probe, threshold and window as a reviewed value per environment; apply the service's own Flyway sequence in order and take every later number from that sequence; release the admin operations on a second colour behind the gateway-bff route and move the traffic only after the synthetic load, approve and listing check passes; read the flags from the platform library and hold no flag value in a chart. No business value is deployed and no message is added.

title: Open points of the intake shadow run on the service: login, route, the legacy criterion AC5 of the integration slice and the P5 contract row
source: Legacy RWB-E1-059 sections 3, 7, 10, 12 and 15; RWB-P5-E1053-CON as the document contract; Arch v5 slides 16, 20 and 41; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5, §R5.7 and §R7.2
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 9 State transitions; 10 Authority; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 15 Screens and states; 18 Traceability
description: The sources leave five points open for the app slice of this key. (1) The login of the rwb-agent service is not named in any source, so the story names it 'the rwb-agent login (DP-02)'. (2) The path of the gateway-bff route in front of the admin reads on /api/recovery/agent/v1 is not named. (3) The legacy criterion AC5 (stale input flagged from a COMPLETED ALS row) is assigned by the split to the integration slice of this key, RWB-ITG-E1059-ITG (wave 1), and not to this app story; the story records it as not owned and does not reconstruct it, and one test case id of the key, TC-E1-059-05, is carried with its legacy data only pending its -ITG copy in that story. (4) The document read of P5 rwb-document is consumed by the intake input set, but the 'Contract dependencies' row of this key is fixed to the three P3 contracts, so the P5 contract is consumed as a C-class contract with its fake and adds no build dependency (DP-11). (5) The sample and evaluation operations are baselined in RWB-P10-E1058-CON, so this story declares no operation of its own and the ownership of those two operations between the platform story and the evaluation story of the same epic stays a documentation point.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-059 section 3 lists 'RWB-E1-030, RWB-E1-058 and RWB-TE-013' as its dependencies and section 12 names POST and GET /admin/agent-evaluations as new in RWB-E1-058; Arch v5 slide 41 gives rwb-agent the first API path /agent-runs/{id} and slide 20 gives every service its own login; the split record of this key lists AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC6, AC7 and AC8 for this app story and assigns AC5 to RWB-ITG-E1059-ITG.
proposed: Agree the service login with the ACE database team; name the route with the edge owner; keep AC5 and its TC-E1-059-05 with RWB-ITG-E1059-ITG, where the split places them; add RWB-P5-E1053-CON to the contract dependency row of a later version when it is published; agree with the evaluation story of the epic which story serves the sample and evaluation operations.

title: Open points of the intake run contract: the start path, four consumed read paths and the field-level members
source: Legacy RWB-E1-059 section 12; TSD P10 v2 Appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; Arch v5 slides 16, 41 and 42 row 01; Ownership Map v1 (agent_run, agent_policy, agent_prompt, agent_sample, agent_evaluation_run, agent_evaluation)
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.8 Contract fakes; 15 Screens and states; 19 Out of scope
description: The sources leave four points open for the contract slice of this key. (1) No source names a start operation for an agent run: Arch v5 slide 41 gives the first API path /agent-runs/{id} and slide 16 gives the AgentRunWorkflow, so the start is declared as POST /agent-runs below the base and the path is marked with the placeholder. (2) The paths of the parameters resolve operation of rwb-case and of the read_accounts, read_valuations and read_contact_points tool reads of rwb-source-data are not named by any source, so each cell carries the placeholder and the fake is written to the assumed shape. (4) The name and path of the gateway-bff route in front of the base are not named.

title: Intake agent evaluation and L1 proposal in rwb-agent: service login, owner of the minimum sample, split of the evaluation operations, route path, source of the three lists and the promotion flag
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-061; Template and Rules v1 R3, R5.5 and R5.7; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.7; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41 and 43; Ownership Map (tables and API of P3, P4 and P10)
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states; 18 Traceability
description: The sources leave six values for this app story open. (1) The login name of the rwb-agent service under DP-02 is named by no document. (2) The owner of the minimum sample of an autonomy step: the legacy story BR3 says it is set in the policy loader schema, while the realignment reads parameters through the rwb-case parameters contract (DP-06), and the minimum 200 for agent INTAKE therefore moves from a schema value to a versioned parameter row. (3) The split of the evaluation operations between the two app stories of the service: the legacy RWB-E1-061 owns only the report operation and the two configuration operations, while RWB-P10-E1060-APP built the start and the read of an evaluation, and the extracted sources list the whole operation set under one module. (4) The route name and path of the gateway-bff route in front of the report read and the two configuration operations (DP-19). (5) The source of the mode and status values: the legacy story treats LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS and LOV-EVAL-STATUS as code enumerations while DP-07 gives reference data to rwb-case. (6) The owner of the legacy feature flag rwb.agent.promotion, which the R-PREC default ruling gives to the platform library and not to the service. The story keeps the legacy behaviour and settles each item by an assumption so that the app work can start; none of the six changes a business value.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-061 section 3 (policy INTAKE P1 in force), section 6 (no login), section 8 BR3 'assumed; set in the policy loader schema', section 12 (three operations on the legacy monolith base) and section 13 (feature flag rwb.agent.promotion); Template and Rules v1 R4 (one login per service), R5.5 DP-02, DP-06, DP-07, DP-13, DP-15 and DP-19, and R3 default rulings (parameters and reference data to P3 rwb-case, feature flags to the platform library); FSD P10 v3 A2.7 and the message set MSG-P10-001 and MSG-P10-008; TSD P10 v2 T3.2 (the three lists) and T-A.1 (API-P10-006 to API-P10-008); Arch v5 slide 16 (P10 IN and OUT) and slide 41 (rwb-agent row); Ownership Map (agent_policy owned by P10, parameter_value and reference_row owned by P3)
owner_role: Solution architect, with the rwb-case owner and the platform library owner
proposed: Settle the six values with their owners and rewrite the six places of this story with them; no behaviour changes, so the disposition stays Moved (no impact)

title: Intake agent evaluation contract: name of an evaluation-completed event, nested types of the promotion members, type detail of the report members and the route path in front of the operations
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-061 section 12; RWB-E1-058 message set; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 and T-A.2; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 42 and 43 (event catalogue); Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.5
section: 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states; 19 Out of scope
description: The sources leave four contract elements of this key open. (1) No source names an event for the completion of an evaluation run: the agent topic rwb.agent.events.v1 carries one business event, rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1 (EV-28), and the completion of an evaluation is only a row state, so the contract declares no event and a name invented for it would be an unowned event type. (2) The internal member names and types of promotion_conditions and watch_measures beyond the three legacy texts (the condition, the fallback and the measures) are not specified; TSD T3.1 gives jsonb only. (3) The type and length of the report members beyond the legacy member list (agent, sampleSize, agreementByLabel[], failureCounts, totalCostThb, costPerCaseThb, latencyP50Ms, latencyP95Ms) are not specified, and the legacy story names the resource without a schema. (4) The route name and path of the gateway-bff route in front of the three provided operations are not specified. The contract fixes the member names and leaves the nested types and the route to the review with their owners; it adds no business value and no behaviour.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-061 section 12 (AgentEvaluationReport member list, no schema) and section 14 (MSG-P10-008, MSG-P10-001, MSG-P7-002); TSD P10 v2 T3.1 (DF-AGT-017 to DF-AGT-020 jsonb and varchar(20)) and T-A.2 API-P10-006 to API-P10-008; Arch v5 slide 43 row 28 (AgentRunCompleted, producer rwb-agent, topic rwb.agent.events.v1) and slide 42 notes (CloudEvents, BACKWARD compatibility); Template and Rules v1 R4 (topic and event naming) and R5.5 DP-14; FSD P10 v3 message set
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-agent, with the solution architect and the platform library owner
proposed: Agree the four elements with their owners at the contract review and rewrite this document and the fakes with them; no behaviour changes

title: The screening slice in rwb-agent: the run-start path, the parameter and ledger operation paths, the two added events, the screening feature flag, the boundary status of a failed tool call and the route in front of the reads are not fixed by any source
source: Legacy RWB-E1-062 sections 3, 4, 5, 11, 12, 13 and 15; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.8 (FEAT-AGT-08) and A2.1 to A2.3 (BR-P10-001 to BR-P10-003); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 (DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-111), T3.2, T5.2, T5.3 and T-A.1 to T-A.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 15, 16, 41, 42, 43 and the call matrix; Ownership Map v1 (agent_run, agent_policy, agent_prompt, agent_sample, agent_evaluation_run, agent_evaluation owner P10; interaction and efs_ledger_outcome owner P1; deviation owner S8; rule_row owner P7; GET /cases/{caseId} owner P3); Template and Rules v1 §R3, §R4, §R5.5 and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC9; 9 State transitions; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.3; 12.8; 13; 15 Screens and states
description: Seven values the rwb-agent slice of this key needs are absent or unresolved in the sources. (1) The legacy screening run is started by an in-process orchestrator call, and no source names a run-start operation: TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 lists eleven P10 operations and none of them starts a run, and Arch v5 slide 16 names only GET /agent-runs/{id} and GET/POST /agent-policies, so the path below the base, the request members and the refusal codes of the start are open. (2) The legacy story reads case, ledger, documents and rule rows through in-process interfaces, and no source names the rwb-source-data operation that returns the interaction ledger or the rwb-case parameters operation for the confidence floor, the look-back and the ledger window, while DP-01 and DP-18 forbid a table read. (3) The event catalogue names only AgentRunCompleted (EV-28) on rwb.agent.events.v1, while a run started and a proposal raised have no catalogued event and no published payload, yet the target story needs both facts to be observable. (4) rule_row belongs to P7 in the Ownership Map while the patterns of this key list no C row for RWB-P7-E1073-CON, so the rule-model read path and its dependency class are open. (5) The legacy feature flag rwb.agent.screening-shadow has no home beyond the §R3 default ruling that feature flags are a platform library. (6) A consumed contract that does not answer has no legacy status: LOV-AGENT-RUN offers TOOL_UNAVAILABLE and FSD A2.9 uses it for an unavailable document interface, but no source states the status, the fallback and the counting for this agent. (7) The gateway-bff route in front of the run read and the evaluation read has no name, path or scope. The story keeps every legacy value and settles each open value as an assumption.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-062 section 3 (policy SCREENING P1, prompt PR1, sample SCREEN-S1 version 1), section 4 ('calls the orchestrator for agent SCREENING with key SCREENING:<caseId>:<eventId>'), section 5 (exception paths X1 to X7), section 12 ('Interfaces called: P3 CaseQueryService.getCase, P7 InteractionLedgerReader.list(caseId, from, to), P5 DocumentQueryService.listByCase and getFields, P3 RuleEvaluator.ownerFor'), section 13 ('Database: migration V10_005__evaluation_review_count.sql', 'Feature flag: rwb.agent.screening-shadow') and section 15; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.1 (API-P10-001 to API-P10-011, no run start) and T3.2 (LOV-AGENT-RUN includes TOOL_UNAVAILABLE); FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.9 AC-EXC-P10-009-01 (TOOL_UNAVAILABLE and fallback true); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (rwb-agent IN and OUT lines), slide 42 row 16 (DocumentStored consumers rwb-agent and rwb-case), slide 43 row 28 (AgentRunCompleted only) and the call matrix (P10 row: R E to P3, R E to P5, R to P1); Ownership Map v1 (interaction owner P1 with the default ruling of §R3 and DP-18; rule_row owner P7); Template and Rules v1 §R3 default ruling, §R4 and §R5.5 DP-01, DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-13, DP-18, DP-19 and DP-20
area: Agent runtime: screening run, consumed reads, events, feature flag and screen route
owner_role: Solution architect with the P10 service owner and the owners of rwb-source-data, rwb-deviation, rwb-case, rwb-document and rwb-decision
proposed: Keep every legacy value and the shadow behaviour; start the run through one operation on the base /api/recovery/agent/v1 fixed by the contract of this key; read the case and the parameters and lists through rwb-case, the open deviations through rwb-deviation, the ledger through rwb-source-data and the documents through rwb-document, each one hop with a 2 s budget; evaluate the owner role in the embedded kit and fetch the package through the rule-model read of RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; publish run started, run completed and proposal raised on rwb.agent.events.v1 through the outbox with the registry subject and the .dlt route; keep the feature flag as a platform row; map a failed consumed read to TOOL_UNAVAILABLE with fallback true and no retry; and reach the reads through the gateway-bff route. Every value is settled in the assumption rows cited and no literal is invented.

title: The screening contract slice: the run-start path and request members, the member types of the proposal payload, the two added event names and payloads, the consumed paths no source names and the route name are not specified by any source
source: Legacy RWB-E1-062 section 12 (the published interfaces, the event published and the output schema screening-v1, the two admin paths); FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.8 and A2.1; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2, T5.3 and T-A.1 to T-A.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 15, 16, 41, 42 and 43; Ownership Map v1 (P10 operations, EV-28, agent tables, interaction ledger); Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.5 and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC7; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.3; 12.8; 13; 19 Out of scope
description: Six elements of the contract slice are open in the sources. (1) The run-start operation that replaces the in-process orchestrator call has no published path below the base, no declared request body and no refusal code set; the eleven P10 operations of TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 carry no start operation. (2) The legacy output schema screening-v1 names proposals of code, reasons, source references, preceding contact and confidence, but no source gives the type or the length of the reasons array and of the source references, the member name of the preceding contact or the type of the marker. (3) The event catalogue names AgentRunCompleted only, so the names and the payloads of a run started and a proposal raised on rwb.agent.events.v1 are taken from the agent_run and proposal fields of TSD P10 v2 T3.1 and not from a published schema. (4) The rwb-source-data ledger operation and the rwb-case parameters operation have no path in any source. (5) The owner role is a rule_row output of P7, and this key lists no C row for RWB-P7-E1073-CON, so the consumed shape is the kit's package rather than a declared REST operation of this story. (6) The gateway-bff route in front of the two operations has no name, path or scope.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-062 section 12 ('Output schema screening-v1: proposals (array of {code in X1..X7, reasons (array of strings, masked), sourceRefs (interaction or document IDs), precedingContactId (X1 only), confidence})', 'Event published: EV-28 AgentRunCompleted', 'Interfaces called: P3 CaseQueryService.getCase, P7 InteractionLedgerReader.list, P5 DocumentQueryService.listByCase and getFields, P3 RuleEvaluator.ownerFor', 'POST and GET on the legacy monolith admin paths'); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 (DF-AGT-046 to DF-AGT-050, DF-AGT-049 output jsonb), T3.2 (LOV-AGENT-RUN, LOV-AUTONOMY) and T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (rwb-agent IN and OUT) and slide 43 row 28 (AgentRunCompleted on rwb.agent.events.v1, consumers rwb-decision, rwb-document and rwb-deviation); Template and Rules v1 §R4 (event name pattern) and §R5.5 DP-04, DP-09, DP-11, DP-13, DP-18 and DP-19
area: Contract: screening operations, proposal payload, event payloads and consumed shapes
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-agent with the solution architect and the owners of rwb-case, rwb-deviation, rwb-source-data, rwb-document and rwb-decision
proposed: Fix one run-start and one run-read operation on the base /api/recovery/agent/v1 with the request members and the answer resource of this document; keep every legacy member of screening-v1 and leave the member types to the review with their owners; declare the three event payloads from the agent_run and proposal fields of TSD P10 v2 T3.1 with the case ID as key, the registry subject and the .dlt route; declare the consumed paths that their owners publish and mark the three that no source names with the placeholder; and declare the route as a pass-through of one hop. The app story and its tests build against these shapes and the seven fakes.

title: Agent monitoring dashboard in rwb-agent: the data lake of the legacy story is removed, and the schedule name, the service login, the route path, the notification operation and the home of the daily aggregate are not specified
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-063 sections 2, 3, 4, 11, 12, 13 and 15; Recovery Workbench Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-10 and DP-17 and §R6 (RWB-E1-014 retired); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 37 (no data lake, INT-19 and INT-20 removed), slide 16 (P10 rwb-agent), slide 31 (measures 01:30 from its own projections) and slide 44 (JOB-15, Airflow trigger, no data lake); FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.6; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 and T-A.2 API-P10-009; Ownership Map v1
section: 2. Business rationale; 3. Preconditions; 4. Flow; 7. Acceptance criteria AC3 and AC4; 12.2, 12.3, 12.6 and 12.7; 13. Solution plan; 15. Screens and states; 18. Traceability
description: The legacy story is written around a data lake that no longer exists, and five values the target needs are named by no source. (1) The data lake is removed by Architecture v5 slide 37, ADR-018 and DP-17, and with it the legacy table agent_run_daily, the nightly copy path of RWB-E1-014 (retired under §R6), the interface INT-20 and the Power BI read of the copy; the legacy requirement REQ-DRI-009 still reads 'copied to the data lake copy daily for reporting, with row counts matched', so the requirement text and the story disagree with the target architecture. (2) No source names the Temporal Schedule that replaces the Quartz entry of JOB-15 for the agent step: slide 44 gives JOB-15 to rwb-reporting as an Airflow trigger with no data lake, and slide 31 gives a 01:30 measures Schedule to rwb-reporting from its own projections, so the agent-side rollup has a time and a behaviour but no name and no owner recorded. (3) The login name of the rwb-agent service under DP-02 is not specified. (4) The path of the gateway-bff route in front of the metric read is not specified. (5) The operation of rwb-comms that carries MSG-P10-004 and the data steward alert is not named by any source. The story keeps the legacy behaviour, keeps every count, date, cost and message ID, replaces the lake write with the event feed into rwb-reporting, and settles each open value as an assumption.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-063 section 2 ('copies daily agent run figures to the data lake'), section 3 ('RWB-E1-014 is done: the nightly copy path to the data lake exists'), section 4 steps 4 and 5, section 11 (no agent_run_daily row, the fields are agent_run and agent_alert), section 12 ('Output: data lake table agent_run_daily', 'Quartz schedule of JOB-15', 'POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun'), section 13 ('migration V10_006__agent_alert.sql', 'Agent monitor v1 Power BI report | One page per agent ... built by RW-BIANAL on agent_run_daily') and section 15 (the Power BI report states); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 37 ('Data lake and Power BI feed (INT-19/20) - Removed: reports from rwb-reporting'), slide 31 ('measures 01:30 (rwb-reporting, JOB-15, from its own projections: no data lake)') and slide 44 ('JOB-15 | Reporting extract | 01:30 | rwb-reporting | Airflow trigger (no data lake)'); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-17 and §R6 (RWB-E1-014 retired, RWB-TE-007 replaced by RWB-PLT-E1071); Business Requirements Program v4 and Epic 1 v4 row REQ-DRI-009; Ownership Map api rows GET /admin/agent-metrics, GET /admin/agent-runs and GET /cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs under P10 and GET /reports/measures under P9; Ownership Map tables agent_alert, agent_run, agent_evaluation under P10 with no daily aggregate table
proposed: Keep the legacy behaviour and its values, and replace the removed lake with the reporting feed that Architecture v5 gives it: the daily aggregate is computed and served by rwb-agent from its own agent_run and agent_evaluation rows in rwb_agent on GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-metrics, the feed into rwb-reporting is rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1 (EV-28) on rwb.agent.events.v1, the nightly trigger is the Temporal Schedule AgentRunDailyRollup on the queue rwb-agent at the legacy 01:30 with overlap SKIP and the one-business-date catch-up window, and the count check of legacy AC3 holds the date of the feed instead of a lake publish. No lake table, extract, credential or INT-19/INT-20 path is created anywhere; the legacy job table and its admin read are not used. Each open value is carried by ASM-B-P10-01-E1063-1 to ASM-B-P10-01-E1063-6 and is confirmed at the wave 1 contract freeze. REQ-DRI-009 should be reworded at the next BRD version to name the event feed and not the lake copy.

title: Agent monitoring contract in rwb-agent: the page size and cursor, the member types of the aggregate element, the held-date status members, the Schedule name, the route path and the notification operation are not specified
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-063 sections 4, 11 and 12; Recovery Workbench Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-09, DP-10, DP-11, DP-13, DP-17 and DP-19; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.2 API-P10-009 and API-P10-010; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 37, 42, 43 and 44; Ownership Map v1
section: 3. Preconditions; 7. Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC6; 11. Data; 12.1, 12.2, 12.3, 12.6 and 12.8; 15. Screens and states
description: The contract slice needs six values that no source fixes. (1) API-P10-009 names the query agent, segment, version, from and to and the answer AgentMetric[], but no source gives the page size, the cursor form, the maximum page or the member names and types of AgentMetric beyond the figures the legacy story lists. (2) The status of a held business date is new in the target, because the lake publish that carried the hold is removed, so its members and its answer code have no source. (3) No source names the Temporal Schedule that replaces the Quartz entry of JOB-15 for the agent step, nor the workflow identity that makes a rerun idempotent on the business date. (4) The path of the gateway-bff route in front of the metric read is not specified. (5) The rwb-comms operation that carries MSG-P10-004 and the data steward alert is not named. (6) The rwb-reporting measures operation is known by its path only, and the shape of the measure row this key reads is not fixed. The contract keeps the legacy figures and settles each open value as an assumption, and it declares no lake artefact, because none exists.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-063 section 4 step 5 (MSG-P10-004 to the alert role and RW-RISK), section 11 (the field list of agent_run, agent_evaluation and agent_alert) and section 12 (the in-process AgentRunExtractSource, the lake output and the job admin paths); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.2 API-P10-009 ('Request: Query: agent, segment, version, from, to; Response: AgentMetric[]; Errors 401, 403, 422, 503') and API-P10-010; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (P10 OUT topic rwb.agent.events.v1: AgentRunCompleted), slide 37 (no data lake), slide 42 (CloudEvents and the outbox), slide 43 (A3 row 28, producer rwb-agent) and slide 44 (JOB-15, no data lake); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-09, DP-10, DP-17 and DP-19; Ownership Map api rows GET /admin/agent-metrics and GET /reports/measures and tables agent_alert, agent_run, agent_evaluation under P10
proposed: Fix the read on the base /api/recovery/agent/v1 with the five query parameters of API-P10-009 and a declared page size and cursor, the aggregate element with the legacy figures - runs, answered, fallback, fallback rate at four decimals, latency p50 and p95, tokens, cost and the latest evaluation score - and a held-date status carrying the business date, the run state and the previous published date. Declare the Schedule AgentRunDailyRollup in namespace rwb-recovery on the queue rwb-agent with the business date as its identity, the legacy 01:30 cadence, overlap policy SKIP and the one-business-date catch-up window. Restate the run read and the case agent-outputs read from the baseline of RWB-P10-E1058-CON rather than redefining them, declare EV-28 as the only feed of the aggregate, and write four fakes. Each open value is carried by ASM-B-P10-01-E1063-7 to ASM-B-P10-01-E1063-10 and is confirmed at the contract freeze with the owners of rwb-reporting, rwb-comms and the edge.

title: Agent monitoring deployment in rwb-agent: the topology, host, SKU, budget, route path, login, feed retention and alert thresholds are not specified
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-063 sections 3, 4, 5 and 12; Recovery Workbench Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-09, DP-10, DP-17 and DP-19 and §R9; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16, slide 20 and slide 37; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T7; Ownership Map v1
section: 3. Preconditions; 5. Exception paths; 7. Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC8; 10. Authority; 11. Data; 12.2 and 12.6; 13. Solution plan
description: The deployment story needs values that no source carries, and it must not invent one: the cluster names, node pools, replica counts, resource sizes, zone spread, ingress class and exact probe timings; the host, the SKU and the budget of the release; the exact path of the gateway-bff route in front of the metric read; the login name of the rwb-agent service; the retention and the partition detail of rwb.agent.events.v1 and of its retry and .dlt topics, and the relay interval of the outbox; and the thresholds of the four dashboards and the four alerts, including the window after which a sent-empty alert fires and the lag at which the feed alert fires. The legacy story fixes the schedule time 01:30, the message MSG-P10-004, the 15-minute alerting target of NFR-068 and the cost cap of 2,000 baht, and those values are kept as they are; every other number is a value of the environment, not of this story. Each missing value is carried by the placeholder of §R9 and one assumption row.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-063 section 3 ('JOB-15 Reporting extract runs nightly at 01:30'), section 4 (the step, the alert and the notice), section 5 X5 ('retried by JOB-11 Outbox sender'), section 12 (the Quartz schedule and the rerun operation); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (P10 rwb-agent, queue rwb-agent, topic rwb.agent.events.v1), slide 20 (outbox relay in every service) and slide 37 (no data lake); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T7 (NFR-008 under 2 seconds) and T5.3 (AgentRunCompleted published); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-09, DP-10, DP-17, DP-19 and §R9; Ownership Map events EV-28 under P10 and api rows under P10
proposed: Expose every topology value as a chart value and fix only its name and the rule that it is not hard-coded; register the Schedule AgentRunDailyRollup at the legacy 01:30 in namespace rwb-recovery on the queue rwb-agent with overlap SKIP and the one-business-date catch-up window; provision rwb.agent.events.v1 with its retry and .dlt topics and the publish right of rwb-agent, and verify the consume right of rwb-reporting without creating its consumer group; publish the metric read and the two baseline reads behind the gateway-bff pass-through route; wire the four alerts to MSG-P10-004, the held date, the sent-empty path of legacy AC7 and the feed, each with one runbook entry; carry no lake credential, extract file or data-set job, and fail a release that carries one. The values are carried by ASM-B-P10-01-E1063-11 to ASM-B-P10-01-E1063-15 and are fixed per environment at the release review.
